properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 2 at 9:50PM EDT until September 3 at 9:45PM EDT by NWS Buffalo NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...East Central Monroe County in western New York...

* WHEN...Until 945 PM EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of Irondequoit Creek and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. This will include
Ellison Park, with water levels possibly effecting Blossom Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 946 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Flooding is expected on Irondequoit Creek in the
warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.5 inches are possible in
the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Irondequoit, East Rochester, Fairport, Brighton and Penfield.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.description:
...HIGH SURF ADVISORY FOR SOUTH AND SOUTHEAST FACING SHORES
THROUGH THURSDAY...

.Swells from Hurricane Lowell will steadily fill in across rest of
the island chain tonight into Thursday and will produce advisory
level surf for south and southeast exposures throughout the state.
Swells from Lowell will gradually veer from southeast to south
tonight through Thursday. Additionally, a moderate long period
south swell will peak tonight then gradually decline through the
rest of the week.

* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet.

* WHERE...South and southeast exposures of all Hawaiian Islands.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM HST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate. Strong breaking waves and strong currents
will make swimming dangerous.
properties.instruction:

go out.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 2 at 2:27PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
A strong front moves toward the Kuskokwim Delta coast overnight
tonight. Southerly onshore winds gusting up to 40 mph coupled with
a lengthy fetch will promote elevated water levels 1 to 2 feet
above normal high tide late tonight into early Thursday morning.
Strongest winds are expected to peak Thursday morning, with up to
0.5 inches of rainfall. Areas of the coastline that are
perpendicular to the southerly wind direction, such as
Kwigillingok, have a higher chance of seeing impacts with this
front. Strong southerly winds will continue through Thursday
afternoon and evening before slowly diminishing through Thursday
night.

* WHAT...A warm front associated with strong Bering Sea low will
move into Western Alaska Wednesday evening into Thursday, with
widespread rain and gusty winds expected. Water levels late
Thursday through Saturday morning could rise 1 to 2 feet above
the normal high tide line along the Yukon Delta Coast.

gusts across the West Coast will peak on Thursday around 30 to
50 mph, with around 0.50 to 1.25 inches of rain expected through
Thursday night. Winds will be lighter Friday and Saturday, but
will remain onshore.

properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM NOON WEDNESDAY TO 8 PM MDT
THURSDAY DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR EAST BEAVERHEAD...

.Strong southwest winds will develop Wednesday as a cold front tracks
eastward and stalls along the Continental Divide. Winds will peak
each afternoon and early evening. Winds will remain elevated
Wednesday night, especially across midslopes and ridgetops, with poor
humidity recoveries.

The National Weather Service in Missoula MT has issued a Red Flag
Warning in effect from noon Wednesday to 8 PM MDT Thursday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 111.

* TIMING...From noon Wednesday to 8 PM MDT Thursday.

* WINDS...Southwest winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 50 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 20 to 30 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
Please advise the appropriate officials or fire crews in the field of
this Red Flag Warning.

Make and maintain your go kit. Is it ready to go? Are there any
materials you need to refresh? Visit ready.gov/kit.

A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions that
promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening. This
does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either occurring
now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple ways to
receive information from authorities.
